title: Planetary prelude: before there was a local landmass
display_window: Earth formation, approximately 4.54 billion years ago
central_question: What is the earliest meaningful starting point for a history of this material territory?
established_in_this_pass: The Earth-age estimate supplies a planetary frame, not a dated local surface. Keep any origin-of-the-universe prelude optional: the local evidential chain begins with the material and geological history of the planet.
limitations: No rock from the present territory has been shown in this pass to be as old as Earth. Neither current latitude/longitude nor the present coast can be projected unchanged into planetary formation.
research_tasks: Explain measurement versus reconstruction and distinguish global context from local evidence.
Document source edition and uncertainty of the Earth-age estimate.
Link the next dossier to actual samples within the scope, rather than describing all world geology as local history.

title: Ancient crust: sample histories, not the age of a state
display_window: Precambrian; local numerical boundaries pending specialist review
central_question: Which minerals and rocks now within the territory preserve the earliest dated processes?
established_in_this_pass: The Trivandrum Block paper and the later peninsular-crust paper are relevant starting points. They require sample-by-sample interpretation; the 2006 paper has an erratum whose contents remain unread.
limitations: An inherited zircon core, a crystallization age, a metamorphic overgrowth and a model crust-extraction age answer different questions. None alone dates a continuously exposed geographical landmass. Do not publish an oldest-rock ranking from an article title.
research_tasks: Retrieve S002 together with S003 and register every correction.
Build a sample table: locality, coordinates with access restrictions, mineral, analytical spot, method, uncertainty, interpretation and laboratory provenance.
Check S006 full text and later responses; distinguish Hadean ancestry claims from intact-rock formation.
Keep samples outside the scope as geological context, not local finds.

title: Metamorphism and the assembly of Gondwana
display_window: Late Precambrian–early Palaeozoic research frame; not a local calendar
central_question: How did the blocks that now underlie the territory become connected and transformed?
established_in_this_pass: The studied southern block preserves evidence interpreted in relation to Gondwana assembly. The record concerns high-temperature processes and mineral histories, not the current coastline.
limitations: Assembly and breakup are separate episodes. Do not make one age apply to every block, and do not adopt apparent ages from the 2006 abstract before checking its erratum.
research_tasks: Map terranes, shear zones and sample relations using attributable geological mapping.
Compare competing reconstructions and identify the measurement supporting each linkage.
Separate dated metamorphism from inferred plate configuration.
Record reconstruction model version and uncertainty; a moving-rock reconstruction is not a fixed present-day polygon.

title: Continental separation and the western margin
display_window: Mesozoic–early Cenozoic research frame; chronology to be resolved by process
central_question: Which rifting, separation and magmatic episodes affected the ancestors of today’s territory?
established_in_this_pass: The west-coast tectono-magmatic paper is relevant to a multi-stage margin history. It does not justify treating the western margin, Ghats and present beach as one simultaneous creation.
limitations: The earlier outline’s 250-million-year division was editorial, not a dated local event. Exact India–Madagascar separation and later spreading ages have not been verified in this seed.
research_tasks: Retrieve regional plate-kinematic and geochronological studies.
Record separate dates for rift initiation, final separation, seafloor spreading, volcanism and later deformation.
Mark adjacent offshore observations as explanatory context.
Avoid assigning modern continental outlines to all palaeogeographic maps.

title: Western Ghats: uplift, erosion and drainage
central_question: How did relief and drainage evolve, and which observations discriminate among explanations?
established_in_this_pass: Offshore sedimentation has been used to investigate erosion and the development of the western Indian margin. The cited Basin Research article is a 2008 publication.
limitations: No single mountain-range birthday is established. Rock age, surface age, uplift, incision and exhumation cannot be interchanged. A basin-wide inference is not automatically evidence for every local river.
research_tasks: Review thermochronology, erosion histories, geomorphology and dated sediment provenance together.
Create separate records for measurements and the authors’ interpretations.
Map evidence density by watershed; retain disagreements between models.
Build a palaeoclimate and monsoon source list before asserting a detailed climatic chronology.

title: Cenozoic sediments and past life
display_window: Cenozoic; a checked local example is approximately 17 million years ago
central_question: What organisms and environments are preserved in the sedimentary record of the territory?
established_in_this_pass: A study of Quilon Formation molluscan material reports a preferred depositional estimate of 17.08–17.13 Ma. A separate fish-otolith study provides a route into palaeobiological evidence.
limitations: The reported range is not labelled here as a confidence interval. It dates sampled strata as interpreted by the authors, not the entire coastal plain. The otolith paper has different online and volume publication years.
research_tasks: Obtain sample tables, fossil localities, analytical methods and stratigraphic logs.
Track taxonomic revisions with stable specimen identifiers and museum repositories.
Distinguish fossil occurrence, depositional environment and inferred climate.
Keep scientific publication dates in the history-of-research index, not the deep-time column.

title: Quaternary landscapes, sea levels and environments
central_question: How did shorelines, wetlands, rivers and habitats change before and during human occupation?
established_in_this_pass: The repository has not yet assembled a critically reviewed local sea-level or palaeoenvironmental series. This is an explicitly open dossier, not a filled gap.
limitations: The present beach, backwaters and river mouths must not be treated as stationary. A single flood story is not a complete coastal history. Do not give unsourced dates to the birth of a lagoon or the destruction of a port.
research_tasks: Inventory dated cores, pollen, charcoal, sedimentary facies and geomorphological studies.
Separate global sea-level context from measured local relative sea level.
Record reservoir corrections, sediment reworking and age-depth model uncertainty.
Retrieve a versioned chronostratigraphic chart before importing formal numerical boundaries.
Cross-link later flood accounts to independent sedimentary evidence without presuming agreement.

title: Earliest reported hominin presence
display_window: Lower Palaeolithic attribution reported; absolute local onset unresolved
central_question: What is the earliest securely contextualized evidence for hominin activity inside the scope?
established_in_this_pass: The 2016 north-Kerala study’s accessible abstract suggests occupation from the Lower Palaeolithic. It is a research lead beyond the Edakkal rock-art discussion.
limitations: The full report and a secure earliest absolute date were not obtained. Typological classification is not a calendar date. The presence of stone tools does not on its own identify their makers as Homo sapiens.
research_tasks: Retrieve the complete report and all cited earlier field studies.
Distinguish excavated stratified finds from surface and redeposited finds.
Record raw material, typology, depositional context, geochronology and site condition.
Maintain separate claims for artefact identification, cultural attribution, dating and species assignment.

title: Later stone-tool communities and shelters
display_window: Mesolithic labels and local transitions; dates require individual evaluation
central_question: What do shelter deposits and tool assemblages reveal without forcing a pan-regional sequence?
established_in_this_pass: The teaching overview identifies Thenmala/Tenmala and Ankode as relevant stratified shelter contexts and points to earlier research.
limitations: The overview’s 5210-years-ago statement cannot be converted into a precise BCE year without the original measurement and calibration. Its description is not a warrant to label every Kerala Mesolithic assemblage microlithic.
research_tasks: Retrieve the cited Rajendran reports and identify laboratory numbers.
Preserve original BP values, uncertainty, calibration curve, material and context.
Compare flake technologies and microliths rather than assuming one diagnostic toolkit.
Document food remains, seasonality and mobility only where deposits support them.

title: Edakkal and other rock art
display_window: Undated or broadly attributed panels; do not assign all figures to 6000 BCE
central_question: Which marks belong to which phases, and how can their ages be constrained?
established_in_this_pass: A tourism page makes the 6000 BCE claim. The scholarly discussion inspected does not establish that date as a secure absolute date for the engravings.
limitations: This is not proof that a particular proposed early date is false. Nearby celts, later inscriptions, stylistic parallels and superimposition provide different types of information. Interpretations of figures and beliefs must remain attributed.
research_tasks: Create panel- and motif-level records with survey provenance.
Separate engravings from inscriptions and document their physical relationships.
Review direct dating claims and associated-context dating critically.
Record local knowledge and later documentation history without declaring colonial documentation the first awareness of the site.

title: Food production, settlement and changing livelihoods
display_window: Site-specific later-prehistoric transitions; no uniform onset assigned
central_question: When and where are cultivation, domestication or more sedentary residence actually evidenced?
established_in_this_pass: This pass has not established a dated, territory-wide Neolithic or farming transition. The earlier chapter was a research proposal, not a demonstrated chronology.
limitations: A polished stone implement does not by itself establish a farming village or domesticated crop. Evidence from neighbouring regions is context until a local connection is demonstrated.
research_tasks: Inventory archaeobotanical, zooarchaeological, residue and settlement evidence.
Distinguish wild use, cultivation and domestication.
Check intrusive material and directly dated specimens.
Retain different livelihood combinations and regional chronologies rather than narrating an inevitable progression.

title: Iron Age, burials and early settlement
display_window: Local later-prehistoric and early-historic sequences overlap
central_question: How do burial assemblages, iron use, habitation and exchange relate in specific places?
established_in_this_pass: The KCHR handbook assigns an approximate 1000–500 BCE Iron Age phase to Pattanam. The official archaeological retrospective is a route to early studies of burial monuments.
limitations: One site’s phase is not a date for all megaliths. Monument type is not a direct ethnic label; iron in a burial does not date the first introduction of iron to the whole territory.
research_tasks: Inventory excavated graves and habitation sites separately.
Capture stratigraphy, sample dates, assemblages, disturbance and excavation season.
Connect metallurgy, agriculture and social interpretations only with stated evidence.
Retain burial terminology from the source alongside a normalized typology.

title: First documentary horizon: references to southwestern polities
display_window: Third century BCE; initial annual navigation begins at 300 BCE
central_question: What does each early textual witness actually attest, and how is its geography identified?
established_in_this_pass: Rock Edict II names Keralaputras in the inspected translation. Its editorial note proposes 257 BCE; the present index conservatively preserves a third-century horizon and the proposed year separately.
limitations: 300 BCE is an indexing boundary, not a claim of an event or the beginning of literacy. An external reference is not an inscription found within the scope, and a named polity is not an exact modern boundary.
research_tasks: Inspect Hultzsch and later critical editions, scripts, readings and inscription locations.
Compare earlier textual candidates without treating traditional narrative dates as composition dates.
Document arguments connecting Keralaputras with Cheras and map the uncertainty.
Extend annual navigation earlier when warranted; do not enforce a fixed earliest-history dogma.

title: Early historic communities and Indian Ocean connections
display_window: Approximately 300 BCE–500 CE as an editorial research window
central_question: How do texts, settlements, imports and local production illuminate distinct communities?
established_in_this_pass: The Periplus describes ports and trade; Pattanam provides archaeological evidence to compare with textual geography. Each has its own dating and interpretative constraints.
limitations: Approximate composition, excavation phases and specimen dates must remain distinct. Do not equate Pattanam and Muziris as a settled identity or assign Sangam poems a single exact year.
research_tasks: Build poem-level Sangam witnesses and a critical-translation registry.
Retrieve Pliny and Ptolemy passages with exact book/section locators.
Add numismatics, inscriptions, archaeobotany and settlement reports.
Separate imported objects from assumptions about the ethnicity or nationality of residents.

title: Regional institutions, languages and networks
display_window: Approximately 501–1497 CE; editorial window, not one social stage
central_question: How did locally varied political, agrarian, linguistic and religious institutions change?
established_in_this_pass: The Kollam-plates research project demonstrates why proposal text, final interpretation and critical edition must be distinguished. It provides one carefully qualified medieval seed, not a complete chronology.
limitations: No single birth year for a language or a whole religious community is established. Genealogies, retrospective legends and regnal calculations require individual review.
research_tasks: Prioritize copper plates and stone inscriptions with photographs, editions and calendrical reasoning.
Cover Chera Perumals, Venad, Kolathunadu, Kozhikode, Kochi and smaller local authorities without imposing a unified kingdom.
Investigate land relations, labour, caste, gender, worship and scholarship together.
Use Arab, Persian, Chinese, Jewish and Christian records with provenance and translation review.

title: Early modern encounters and competing sovereignties
central_question: How did overseas powers interact with existing local institutions and maritime networks?
established_in_this_pass: The voyage journal excerpt places the Portuguese arrival account at Calicut in 1498. The prior Periplus evidence demonstrates that maritime exchange long predates that arrival.
limitations: The year does not mark the discovery of an unknown or uninhabited coast. Accounts by travellers are situated testimony, including misidentification, rhetoric and hostility.
research_tasks: Compare Portuguese records with local, Arabic and other accounts.
Inventory Dutch, French and Mysorean source series and local consequences.
Keep Mahe as external administrative context, linked to relevant in-scope activity.
Treat violence, trade, everyday livelihoods and religious change as intersecting histories, not a simple succession of European powers.

title: Colonial administration, princely institutions and public life
display_window: 1792–1946 CE; editorial window needing local refinements
central_question: Which administrations and communities generated records for different parts of the modern territory?
established_in_this_pass: Archive portals, manuals and later archaeological histories provide source routes. No claim is made that this starter has audited a complete colonial series.
limitations: The chosen window is an organizational convention, not a uniformly verified regime boundary. Gazetteer descriptions and censuses reflect administrative categories and do not speak for every community.
research_tasks: Inventory district manuals, revenue proceedings, censuses, gazettes, court records and newspapers by volume and year.
Separate British-administered Malabar from Travancore and Cochin institutions.
Study reform, labour, slavery, caste, gender and resistance with multiple independent source traditions.
Do not restrict inclusion to people described as Malayali or records written in Malayalam.

title: Integration and the present-state frame
display_window: 1947–1956 CE; precise legal events require individual dates
central_question: How did administrative reorganization affect the land inside the modern study frame?
established_in_this_pass: The 1956 statute provides a precise appointed day and defines transferred territories. It must be read with its exclusions rather than summarized as all Malabar plus all Travancore-Cochin.
limitations: State formation did not create the land, its inhabitants or all cultural identities. The 1956 Act is not itself a verified current boundary dataset.
research_tasks: Read integration instruments, successive acts and boundary adjustments.
Trace village/taluk-level inclusion and exclusion rather than assuming old and current districts match.
Separate passage, assent, publication and commencement dates.
Record viewpoints and movements behind reorganization using contemporary records.

title: Contemporary territory, environment and society
central_question: How can a living public record be indexed without mistaking availability for completeness?
established_in_this_pass: The verified 2025 manuscript-collection announcement demonstrates that the accessible corpus itself continues to change. It belongs to research and access history, not to the manuscripts’ original production years.
limitations: This seed does not claim a verified contemporary political or economic chronology. Living-person data, allegations, sacred knowledge and sensitive site locations require explicit safeguards.
research_tasks: Inventory official statistical, electoral, environmental and legislative series at item level.
Preserve definitions, territorial coverage and revisions before comparing statistics over time.
Balance public institutions with fisheries, farming, forests, migration, labour, science, culture, gender and marginalized communities.
Track corrections, retractions and access changes; treat 2026 as a partial year.
